Any network indicator must add information \\emph{beyond} these baselines. Network science offers a rich toolkit for studying how information, behaviour and innovations spread through structured populations \\citep{OBrien2018}. In citation and co-authorship networks, knowledge diffusion follows structured pathways that reflect both the topology of the network and the position of the spreading entity within it \\citep{Domenico2016,Renoust2017}. Community structure shapes diffusion outcomes: bridge nodes and boundary-spanning ties accelerate spread across groups \\citep{Cherifi2019,Burt2004}, while community cohesion can either facilitate or retard it depending on the contagion mechanism \\citep{Centola2010,Ugander2012}.\n\nPrior work has proposed several candidate signals for concept diffusion. \\citet{Cheng2023} tracked roughly 2{,}000 new ideas across Web of Science fields and found that early social reach, the number of disconnected researcher groups, was the strongest predictor of whether an idea became ``core.'' Their ideational consistency measure predicted next-year volume. \\citet{Weng2013} showed that early community diversity predicts virality of online content (AUC 0.83). \\citet{Salatino2017} showed that collaboration density rises before topic emergence, and \\citet{Chavalarias2013} used phylomemetic methods to track the branching and merging of scientific fields. \\citet{Gao2018} tracked community evolution in patent co-occurrence networks, revealing how technological change reshapes network structure. \\citet{Sattar2023} developed approaches for detecting the temporal evolution of communities, and \\citet{Callon1991} introduced co-word analysis as a tool for mapping research structure. These studies typically operate on curated concept sets without held-out validation, mix concept-level and field-level units of analysis, or do not control for simple volume-based predictors. No prior study has screened a broad set of temporal knowledge-network indicators against a shared baseline on held-out field groups for the specific outcome of size-adjusted cross-disciplinary breadth.\n\nA second open question concerns the routes by which concepts move between fields. The principle of relatedness, established for regional economic diversification \\citep{Hidalgo2007,Neffke2011,Fitzgerald2021}, predicts that actors diversify into activities related to their existing portfolio. For scientific fields adopting new concepts, this principle has been tested for entry but not for the role of currently \\emph{retaining} fields---those that have adopted a concept and kept publishing on it. Whether concepts spread next to fields related to the ones currently retaining them, beyond relatedness to the home field alone, is untested.\n\nThis paper addresses both questions with a large-scale empirical study. We identify 12{,}499 concepts from the OpenAlex bulk snapshot, compute 53 early network indicators across six families, and test them on held-out field groups and a confirmatory onset cohort. We also build a conditional logit model of field entry that tests whether retained-field relatedness predicts the next field a concept enters. We report the following contributions:\n\n\\begin{enumerate}\n    \\item We screen 53 early co-occurrence network indicators\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_DVtwwCx0JbFq/round-3/experiment-8}} against a five-feature popularity baseline and confirm seven on held-out field groups for predicting rarefied cross-field breadth. Two of the seven carry negative signs: early retention ratio and ego-network density.\n    \\item We introduce the OPEN index, a six-component composite of early co-occurrence openness, and test it on a 2015--2017 cohort never used in selection. A descriptive meta-analysis of OPEN\\textsubscript{home} over six non-selection bodies gives partial Spearman $+0.069$ $[+0.038, +0.100]$, $I^2 = 0$, 6/6 positive; the evidence state is lead.\n    \\item We test whether concepts spread next to fields related to the ones currently retaining them. On an independent frame\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_DVtwwCx0JbFq/round-3/experiment-7}} (11,841 concepts, 6,978 entry events in 6,076 informative strata), the retained-frontier coefficient is $d_0 = +0.322$ $[+0.291, +0.355]$. The pre-registered verdict is FRONTIER = PARTIAL: the volume-matched contrast is null, the coefficient reverses under minimum-conditional-probability proximity, and the held-out dose response is not monotone. Persistence and volume remain confounded.\n    \\item We show that early neighbourhood consolidation, measured by \\citeauthor{Cheng2023}'s (\\citeyear{Cheng2023}) ideational consistency, predicts volume growth but \\emph{narrower} cross-field reach, a reversal that holds in all five field groups.\n    \\item We decompose breadth into exploration and retention channels and show that early contact diversity accounts for 73\\% of the breadth gap. No discrete trajectory typology passes the naming rule; diffusion paths form a continuum along a breadth axis.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\n\n\\section{Methods}\n\\label{sec:methods}\n\n\\subsection{Concept identification and panel construction}\n\nWe use the OpenAlex bulk snapshot (2026-09-23; 476{,}196{,}327 works; 129.4 million base works 1995--2022). Concepts are identified by Aho--Corasick title matching of 56{,}643 legacy OpenAlex concepts (levels 2--5) plus Wikidata aliases, with stemmed verification. A per-concept LLM precision gate drops concepts with precision below 0.80.\n\nA concept's \\emph{onset year} $t_0$ is the first year it reaches 20 grounded publications. \\emph{Home field(s)} are the field(s) holding at least 40\\% of the first 30 grounded papers. The specification was frozen on DEV data (hash-sealed before held-out scoring) and unsealed once. The panel comprises 12{,}499 concepts and 27{,}393 concept-by-field adoption episodes (Table~\\ref{tab:panel}).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Panel composition. DEV concepts have home fields in Computer Science, Engineering, Biochemistry/Genetics/Medicine. Held-out groups cover the remaining field families.}\n\\label{tab:panel}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lrr}\n\\toprule\nSplit & Concepts & Episodes \\\\\n\\midrule\nDEV (CS/Eng/BGM/Med, onset 2003--2009) & 4{,}771 & 9{,}079 \\\\\nCohort (onset 2010--2014, all fields) & 4{,}356 & 9{,}799 \\\\\nHeld-out Physical Sciences & 742 & 1{,}662 \\\\\nHeld-out Life \\& Environment & 1{,}113 & 3{,}099 \\\\\nHeld-out Social Sciences & 1{,}352 & 3{,}320 \\\\\nHeld-out Math \\& Decision Sci. & 165 & 434 \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\textbf{Total} & \\textbf{12{,}499} & \\textbf{27{,}393} \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\subsection{Outcome: rarefied field breadth}\n\nThe primary outcome is \\emph{rarefied field breadth} $O_{2r}$ ($m = 50$): the expected number of distinct venue fields among a fixed-size random draw of $m$ papers from a concept's publications in years $t_0 + 6$ to $t_0 + 8$, computed by exact hypergeometric rarefaction. Rarefaction separates size-adjusted breadth from sheer volume. Secondary outcomes include sustained uptake ($O_{1c}$), transience ($O_3$), and field- and year-normalised citation growth ($O_4$).\n\n\\subsection{Baseline and indicator families}\n\\label{sec:indicators}\n\nWe define a \\emph{five-feature baseline} (B5) consisting of log early volume, publication growth, non-home share, Shannon entropy and field reach, all computed over $t_0$ to $t_0 + 2$. The 53 candidate indicators span six families:\n\n\\begin{enumerate}\n    \\item \\textbf{Co-occurrence ego-network (A, 27 indicators):} degree, density, persistence, novelty, community counts, participation, brokerage from the concept's ego network on the co-occurrence backbone.\n    \\item \\textbf{Popularity and volume (E, 6 indicators):} publication growth, author growth, author count.\n    \\item \\textbf{Disciplinary spread (F, 3 indicators):} Shannon entropy of field distribution, home-field relatedness, Rao--Stirling diversity.\n    \\item \\textbf{Retained frontier (FR, 7 indicators):} contact reach, retention ratio, RCA-based and volume-weighted field densities.\n    \\item \\textbf{Gateway centrality (G, 7 indicators):} eigenvector centrality of home and early off-home fields on the field backbone.\n    \\item \\textbf{Co-author reach (S, 3 indicators):} author overlap with other concepts, connected components among co-authors.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\n\\subsection{The OPEN index}\n\nThe OPEN index is the mean of six signed $z$-scored ego-network components from the early window ($t_0$ to $t_0 + 2$):\n\n\\begin{enumerate}\n    \\item New edge rate (positive sign): the fraction of a concept's co-occurrence neighbours that are new.\n    \\item Number of Leiden communities reached ($n_{\\text{comm}}$, positive): how many distinct topic communities a concept's neighbours span.\n    \\item Participation coefficient (positive): the share of a concept's ties that cross community boundaries.\n    \\item Neighbourhood novelty residual (NOV\\textsubscript{res}, positive): the novelty of a concept's co-occurrence partners after residualising on degree.\n    \\item Ego density (negative sign): the density of the concept's local co-occurrence subgraph.\n    \\item Edge persistence (negative sign): the fraction of the concept's neighbours retained across windows.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\nThe $z$-score constants are frozen from the DEV data. We test three builds: OPEN\\textsubscript{home} (home-field co-occurrence graph only), OPEN\\textsubscript{all} (corpus-wide graph), and OPEN\\textsubscript{sizematch} (corpus-wide papers subsampled to home counts).\n\n\\subsection{Statistical framework}\n\nIndicator screening uses \\emph{partial Spearman priority} (PSP): the Pearson correlation of rank-transformed indicator and outcome residuals, both residualised on the baseline covariates and control rungs. Inference uses 2{,}000 concept-level bootstrap resamples with refit. Pooling across field groups uses the DerSimonian--Laird random-effects estimator \\citep{Dersimonian1986} with $I^2$ heterogeneity reporting \\citep{Higgins2002}. Multiple comparisons use Holm correction across the pre-declared family.\n\nWe also define NOVCHURN as the mean of $z(\\text{NOV}_{\\text{res}})$ and $-z(\\text{edge persistence})$, a two-component novelty/churn measure used in mechanism analyses.\n\n\\subsection{Field-entry model (RQ2)}\n\nFor the field-entry analysis, we use a conditional logit (Breslow partial likelihood) on concept-year risk sets, stratified by concept-year, with standardised covariates: relatedness to home, log field size, density over entered fields, gateway centrality (baseline R0); RCA-based density (R1); volume-weighted density (R2); and retained-field relatedness $d_0$ (R3). A field is ``retaining'' a concept when it has published at least two grounded papers on the concept in each of the two most recent years. Relatedness is measured by positive pointwise mutual information (PMI) on the field-level backbone. The specification is frozen on DEV and scored once on the independent held-out frame.\n\n\n\\section{Results}\n\\label{sec:results}\n\nThe headline finding is the openness--breadth association: a descriptive meta-analysis of OPEN\\textsubscript{home} over six non-selection bodies gives partial Spearman $+0.069$ $[+0.038, +0.100]$, $I^2 = 0$, 6/6 positive; the evidence state is lead. We present the indicator screen (RQ1) first because it defines the OPEN index.\n\n\\subsection{RQ1: Which early network signals predict cross-field breadth?}\n\n\\subsubsection{Experimental setup}\n\nThe top 10 indicators selected on DEV by partial Spearman priority for rarefied breadth ($O_{2r}$, $m = 50$) were tested once on four held-out field groups and two cohort splits. Confirmation requires Holm-corrected $p < 0.05$ and a 95\\% CI excluding zero on the DerSimonian--Laird pooled estimate. The held-out outcomes had been previously used by two earlier experiments, so the indicator-screen results are robustness checks within the same frame rather than fully independent confirmations. The fresh 2015--2017 cohort is the only body never used in any prior step.\n\n\\subsubsection{Comparison to related work}\n\nPrior network-based diffusion studies in \\emph{Applied Network Science} have examined knowledge flow through citation and co-authorship networks \\citep{Domenico2016,Renoust2017}, community-driven diffusion mechanisms \\citep{Cherifi2019,OBrien2018}, and temporal community evolution \\citep{Sattar2023,Gao2018}. These studies model diffusion at the network level but do not screen concept-level co-occurrence indicators against a held-out validation framework for the specific outcome of size-adjusted breadth. \\citet{Weng2013} showed that early community diversity predicts online virality (AUC 0.83); our study extends this to scientific concepts, where the baseline is much stronger (B5 Spearman 0.65--0.86). \\citet{Cheng2023} found that social reach predicts whether ideas become ``core,'' but did not control for a shared baseline or use held-out field groups. \\citet{Fitzgerald2021} showed that academic knowledge is becoming more localised, motivating the question of which early signals distinguish concepts that overcome this localisation.\n\n\\subsubsection{Results}\n\nSeven of the 53 screened indicators survive held-out validation with Holm correction (Table~\\ref{tab:screen}). These span two families: retained frontier (end-of-window field density, volume-weighted field density, contact reach, retention ratio) and co-occurrence topology (community count, neighbourhood novelty residual, ego density). No centrality or volume-only indicator survives. Two confirmed indicators carry negative signs: the early retention ratio ($-$0.114, concepts with higher early field retention spread \\emph{less} broadly) and ego density ($-$0.102, concepts with denser co-occurrence neighbourhoods spread less).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Held-out indicator screen: the 10 indicators with highest DEV partial Spearman priority for rarefied breadth ($O_{2r}$, $m = 50$), tested on held-out groups. DerSimonian--Laird pooled estimates with 95\\% CI. Confirmed indicators (Holm $p < 0.05$ and CI excluding zero) are marked.}\n\\label{tab:screen}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{llccccc}\n\\toprule\nIndicator & Family & Pooled PSP & 95\\% CI & $I^2$ & Sign & Conf. \\\\\n\\midrule\nM0\\_density\\_end & FR & +0.375 & [+0.279, +0.462] & 0.74 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\nD\\_vol\\_end & FR & +0.307 & [+0.256, +0.356] & 0.10 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\nCONTACT\\_REACH & FR & +0.211 & [+0.161, +0.261] & 0.00 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\n$n_\\text{comm}$ (W3) & A & +0.167 & [+0.063, +0.267] & 0.78 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\nNOV\\textsubscript{res} & A & +0.151 & [+0.044, +0.255] & 0.75 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\nRETENTION\\_RATIO & FR & $-$0.114 & [$-$0.160, $-$0.067] & 0.00 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\nego\\_density (W3) & A & $-$0.102 & [$-$0.151, $-$0.053] & 0.00 & 6/6 & \\textbf{Yes} \\\\\nRao--Stirling & G & $-$0.072 & [$-$0.153, +0.010] & 0.44 & 5/6 & No \\\\\n$G_\\text{btw}$ & G & +0.056 & [$-$0.006, +0.118] & 0.33 & 6/6 & No \\\\\nlog offhome vol. & F & $-$0.089 & [$-$0.171, $-$0.007] & 0.63 & 5/6 & No \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nAbout half of the M0\\_density\\_end and D\\_vol\\_end signal is a pre-onset footprint: on held-out data, the post-onset-only field density attenuates from +0.374 to +0.187 [+0.145, +0.246]. The remaining indicators measure genuinely early structural properties.\n\nAn ElasticNet combining all indicators adds Spearman +0.059 [+0.046, +0.073] over B5 on held-out groups; an Explainable Boosting Machine adds +0.052 [+0.037, +0.067].\n\n\\textbf{OPEN index confirmation.} The OPEN index was tested on a 2015--2017 onset cohort\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_DVtwwCx0JbFq/round-4/experiment-10}} (1{,}443 concepts) never used in any prior screen. We define a six-rung control ladder that tests OPEN's partial Spearman with rarefied breadth under increasingly demanding baselines (Table~\\ref{tab:ladder}).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{OPEN index control ladder on the 2015--2017 confirmatory cohort. PSP = partial Spearman priority with rarefied breadth ($O_{2r}$, $m = 50$), 95\\% concept-bootstrap CI.}\n\\label{tab:ladder}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lccccccc}\n\\toprule\nBuild & R0 & R1 & R2 & R3 & R4 & R5 & $n$ \\\\\n\\midrule\nOPEN\\textsubscript{home} & +.12 & +.10 & +.09 & +.08 & +.07 & +.06 & 573 \\\\\nOPEN\\textsubscript{all} & +.21 & +.18 & +.17 & +.17 & +.15 & +.14 & 630 \\\\\nOPEN\\textsubscript{size} & +.18 & +.15 & +.15 & +.14 & +.12 & +.11 & 591 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nOPEN\\textsubscript{home} passes the primary concept-type rung (R2: PSP = +0.091, 95\\% CI [+0.013, +0.171], Holm $p$ = 0.048) but its DerSimonian--Laird pooled interval includes zero (+0.083 [$-$0.007, +0.173]), making the home-only signal marginal. The paired difference OPEN\\textsubscript{all} minus OPEN\\textsubscript{home} at the footprint rung is +0.093 [+0.016, +0.169]; about half of this gap is paper count (OPEN\\textsubscript{sizematch} minus OPEN\\textsubscript{home} = +0.053 [$-$0.015, +0.117]). OPEN\\textsubscript{all} is partly mechanically coupled to the outcome because early off-home papers that enter the ego network are also papers that determine later breadth.\n\nAn evidence synthesis across six non-selection bodies (four held-out domain groups plus the 2010--2014 and 2015--2017 cohorts) gives a DerSimonian--Laird pooled OPEN\\textsubscript{home} partial Spearman of +0.069 [+0.038, +0.100] with $I^2 = 0$, all six bodies positive. The DEV estimate (+0.109) shows shrinkage of 1.58$\\times$ relative to the non-selection pool.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_evidence_synthesis_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Partial Spearman correlation of OPEN\\textsubscript{home} (home-neighbourhood openness over $t_0$ to $t_0{+}2$) with rarefied cross-field breadth ($O_{2r}$, $m=50$) at ladder rung R2. R2 controls for the five-feature popularity baseline B5 plus onset year, contact reach, concept type, a generic-concept flag and concept level. Blue squares with whiskers show the estimate and 95\\% concept-bootstrap CI (2{,}000 draws) for each of six non-selection bodies: four held-out home groups (Physical Sciences, Life \\& Environment, Social Sciences, Math \\& Decision; onsets 2003--09), the 2010--14 onset cohort and the 2015--17 onset cohort. $n$ is the number of concepts analysed. The black diamond spans the DerSimonian--Laird pooled estimate over these six bodies, $+0.069$ $[+0.038, +0.100]$, $I^2 = 0$, 6/6 positive. The dotted vertical line marks this pooled estimate and the dashed line marks zero. The grey row below the separator is the DEV selection body, on which the index was chosen ($+0.109$ $[+0.073, +0.144]$). It is not pooled, and it is $1.58\\times$ the non-selection pool. Values at right are estimate [95\\% CI]. The association is small and has the same sign in every body, but only the two cohort rows and the pool have CIs above zero individually. All non-selection bodies except the 2015--17 cohort had outcomes read in earlier analyses, so the pool is descriptive rather than confirmatory.}\n  \\label{fig:evidence_synthesis}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\textbf{Vocabulary-free replication (Frame~N).} To address survivorship bias in the legacy concept vocabulary, we mined 636 vocabulary-free phrase-born concepts\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_DVtwwCx0JbFq/round-5/experiment-13}} (2003--2015 onsets). These newborns have 14\\% lower breadth and 89\\% higher transience than legacy concepts. On Frame~N, OPEN\\textsubscript{home} gives PSP +0.117 [+0.020, +0.218] at R3 for $O_{2r}$ ($m = 30$); the frozen verdict is PARTIAL: the R5 confidence interval includes zero (+0.086 [$-$0.009, +0.190]), three of four estimable groups are positive, and the Holm-corrected $p$-value is 0.052. Edge persistence is null on Frame~N ($-$0.013); the signal is carried by neighbourhood novelty (NOV\\textsubscript{res} +0.208 [+0.113, +0.303]).\n\n\\textbf{The consistency--breadth reversal.} We rebuilt \\citeauthor{Cheng2023}'s (\\citeyear{Cheng2023}) ideational consistency on OpenAlex topic co-usage for 12{,}311 concepts. In their design (next-year volume, no current-size control), the model reproduces their estimate: $b = 0.428$ (+53.5\\%/SD). Adding current volume removes almost all of it: +1.3\\% [+0.5\\%, +2.1\\%], a residual-to-raw ratio of 0.021. Net of B5, the partial Spearman of consistency with rarefied breadth is $-$0.069 [$-$0.093, $-$0.047] on the pooled bodies ($I^2 = 0$, 5/5 groups negative), replicating on the 2015--2017 cohort ($-$0.111 [$-$0.197, $-$0.030]). The consistency measure has Spearman +0.77 with edge persistence (Jaccard similarity); it is essentially weighted persistence, confirming that a stable neighbourhood predicts growth but not breadth.\n\n\\subsubsection{Discussion of RQ1}\n\nThe confirmed indicators divide into two groups. Contact reach, retention ratio and the field-density measures capture a concept's position in the inter-field backbone and partly reflect a pre-onset footprint. Community count, neighbourhood novelty and ego density capture the topology of the early home-field co-occurrence neighbourhood. The OPEN index combines these into a single measure of early openness. The practical forecasting gain is small: OPEN\\textsubscript{home} adds only +0.002 Spearman on the fresh cohort. The indicators characterise structural preconditions for broad diffusion rather than providing individually actionable forecasts. Life \\& Environment Sciences show the weakest OPEN signal (PSP +0.042 vs pooled +0.069), warranting domain-specific investigation.\n\n\n\\subsection{RQ2: By what routes do concepts spread across fields?}\n\n\\label{subsec:rq2_entry}\n\\subsubsection{Experimental setup}\n\nWe test whether relatedness to the fields currently retaining a concept predicts which field it enters next, using a conditional logit on concept-year risk sets with an independent frame of 11{,}841 concepts (6{,}978 entry events in 6{,}076 informative strata). The frame excludes all concepts used in the original frame construction. The specification was hash-sealed on DEV before held-out scoring. Pre-registered criteria include: pooled R3 CI above zero, positive in the majority of evaluable groups, volume-matched contrast CI above zero, retained-label permutation null rejected, backbone-rewiring null rejected, and dose-response non-negative.\n\n\\subsubsection{Comparison to related work}\n\n\\citet{Hidalgo2007} showed that product-space relatedness predicts economic diversification; the minimum conditional probability defines the standard proximity. \\citet{Neffke2011} extended the principle of relatedness to regional and technological diversification, and \\citet{Fitzgerald2021} showed how regional knowledge networks shape academic localisation. Our contribution is to test whether relatedness to the set of fields currently \\emph{retaining} a concept predicts entry, beyond relatedness to the home field and conventional density measures. The key methodological distinction is that retention, not mere presence, defines the reference set.\n\n\\subsubsection{Results}\n\nOn the independent held-out frame, the retained-frontier coefficient is $d_0 = 0.322$ [0.291, 0.355] with concept-clustered standard errors (R3 vs R2 likelihood-ratio 325.8, $p < 10^{-70}$). The result is positive in three of three evaluable held-out groups: Physical Sciences +0.148, Life \\& Environment +0.401, Social Sciences +0.297. Mathematics \\& Decision Sciences is null (+0.065 [$-$0.109, 0.239], 165 concepts). DerSimonian--Laird pooled $d_0$ = 0.243 [0.118, 0.368], $I^2 = 0.92$ (Table~\\ref{tab:entry}).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Retained-frontier coefficient ($d_0$) from the conditional-logit model of field entry, by domain group and cohort. The pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL: criterion 5 (volume-matched CI $> 0$) fails.}\n\\label{tab:entry}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\nModel & $d_0$ & 95\\% CI (concept) & LR \\\\\n\\midrule\nDevelopment set & 0.228 & [0.164, 0.291] & 34.5 \\\\\nHeld-out pooled & 0.322 & [0.291, 0.355] & 325.8 \\\\\nPhysical Sciences & 0.148 & [0.078, 0.219] & -- \\\\\nLife \\& Environment & 0.401 & [0.342, 0.460] & -- \\\\\nSocial Sciences & 0.297 & [0.246, 0.348] & -- \\\\\nMath \\& Decision Sci. & 0.065 & [$-$0.109, 0.239] & -- \\\\\n2010--2014 cohort & 0.321 & [0.292, 0.347] & -- \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe retained-frontier coefficient survives the conventional RCA density ($D_{\\text{rca}}$) and a share-weighted current presence density: adding $d_0$ after both rivals gives LR = 34.5 on DEV, and $D_{\\text{rca}}$ is absorbed once $d_0$ enters. All three specificity tests reject their nulls after Holm correction (retained-label permutation $p = 0.001$; backbone-rewiring $p = 0.004$; node-label $p = 0.003$).\n\nHowever, the pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL. The volume-matched contrast (comparing entry rates of retained versus entered-but-not-retained fields in the same volume cell) is null: $-$0.028 [$-$0.105, +0.046] on held-out data ($-$0.008 on DEV; Holm $p$ = 0.76). The dose response by retention age on held-out data is 0.098 / 0.075 / 0.304, which is not monotone. Under minimum-conditional-probability proximity \\citep{Hidalgo2007} instead of PMI, $d_0 = -0.021$ ($p = 0.012$), while RCA density becomes strong (LR 246). Persistence is therefore confounded with volume, and the result is backbone-specific.\n\n\\textbf{Gateway centrality.} Gateway centrality does not predict field retention: on 27{,}393 held-out episodes, the increment is effectively zero ($\\Delta$AUC $-$0.00001, 95\\% CI [$-$0.0006, +0.0003]).\n\n\\textbf{Breadth decomposition.} On 3{,}188 DEV concepts\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_DVtwwCx0JbFq/round-4/experiment-12}}, the breadth gap between the top and bottom $O_{2r}$ terciles decomposes as: early contact diversity 77.9\\%, frontier advance $-$4.6\\% (broad concepts gain new fields at similar rates), and retention 26.8\\%. The difference between exploration and retention is 0.464 [0.407, 0.528]. On the held-out pool excluding Medicine (variant iv), the contact share is 0.633 [0.537, 0.727] and the difference is 0.504 [0.329, 0.679] ($I^2 = 0.76$). These shares are an accounting identity for the breadth outcome, not causal effects, because breadth and contact diversity share papers.\n\n\\textbf{Diffusion trajectories.} No discrete trajectory typology passes the naming rule. DTW $k$-medoids and HMM-based clustering on state sequences give an adjusted Rand index of 0.222. PCA reveals a continuum: PC1 (38.8\\% of variance) is a breadth axis, PC2 (10.7\\%) is a keep-versus-lose axis. Early openness (OPEN) correlates with PC1 beyond B5 (held-out partial 0.120, $I^2 = 0$) but not with PC2 (partial $-$0.07 to $-$0.11).\n\n\\textbf{Sequence and closure tests.} A home-prominence half-peak vs off-home take-off test finds no signal beyond the mechanical lag (DEV excess $-$0.009 [$-$0.015, $-$0.003], held-out +0.011 [0.005, 0.016]). Intersection-born concepts take off later (HR 0.47 [0.42, 0.54]). A within-concept closure test is null on DEV\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_DVtwwCx0JbFq/round-5/experiment-15}} (density PPML $b = -0.070$ [$-$0.180, 0.040]; OPEN\\textsubscript{home} $b = +0.015$ [$-$0.038, 0.069]). On held-out fields, OPEN\\textsubscript{home} is opposite-signed ($-$0.079 [$-$0.146, $-$0.013]). Early openness is a between-concept trait, not a within-concept mechanism.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_entry_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Retained-frontier coefficient $d_0$ (log-odds of entering a field per SD of relatedness to the off-home fields that currently retain the concept) from the conditional-logit entry model (rung R3, controlling for home relatedness, field size, entered density, own gateway centrality, RCA density $D_{\\mathrm{rca}}$ and volume density $D_{\\mathrm{vol}}$), by unit. Circles with bars show point estimates with 95\\% concept-bootstrap confidence intervals. The light-blue row is the development (DEV) set used for selection. Dark-blue rows are the held-out domain groups and the 2010--14 onset cohort. The black diamond is the DerSimonian--Laird random-effects estimate pooled over the four held-out groups, and its width spans its 95\\% CI. The right column prints each estimate and interval; $n$ is the number of concepts in each unit. The dashed line marks $d_0 = 0$. $d_0$ is positive with a CI excluding zero in all three evaluable held-out groups (Physical Sciences 0.148, Life \\& Env.\\ 0.401, Social Sciences 0.297) and in the cohort (0.321). Math \\& Decision ($n = 165$, excluded as underpowered before the freeze) is null (0.065 [$-$0.110, 0.234]). The pooled estimate is 0.243 [0.118, 0.368] with high heterogeneity ($I^2 = 0.92$). The frozen verdict is nonetheless PARTIAL: the pre-registered volume-matched contrast is null, and the effect is specific to the PMI backbone.}\n  \\label{fig:entry}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\subsubsection{Discussion of RQ2}\n\nThe retained-frontier result extends the principle of relatedness to concept adoption. The positive coefficient is large and consistent across three of three evaluable groups, but the PARTIAL verdict limits its interpretation: we cannot fully separate persistence from sustained volume as a predictor of field entry. The effect is also backbone-specific: it holds on the sparse PMI backbone but not under the standard Hidalgo proximity. The breadth decomposition shows that integrating and localised concepts differ primarily in how many fields they contact early, not in how many more fields they enter later. The null closure test and opposite-signed held-out result indicate that openness does not operate as a within-concept mechanism driving diffusion.\n\n\n\\subsection{Confound analysis}\n\\label{sec:confound}\n\nThe openness signal could be an artefact of small yearly samples or of dynamic churn. We tested four null models\\footnote{Code: \\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_DVtwwCx0JbFq/round-5/experiment-16}}:\n\n\\textbf{Fixed-size rarefaction.} Subsampling to 10 home papers per year retains 68\\% of the pooled association. The bias-corrected Chao estimator retains 91\\%.\n\n\\textbf{Within-concept permutation null.} The excess churn over a 200-draw within-concept year-label permutation null is indistinguishable from zero: excess NOVCHURN pooled PSP = +0.008 [$-$0.02, +0.03], compared to raw NOVCHURN = +0.116 [+0.09, +0.14]. The $R^2$ of raw persistence on the permutation-null mean is 0.66. What predicts breadth is a static property of the concept's home-topic partner mix.\n\n\\textbf{Degree-preserving configuration null.} Replacing raw ego density and persistence by curveball configuration $z$-scores raises OPEN\\textsubscript{home} from +0.092 to +0.115.\n\n\\textbf{Reliability.} Split-half reliability of NOVCHURN\\textsubscript{raw} is 0.48. The temporal-excess variants (V2) have split-half Spearman--Brown reliability of approximately 0.01--0.05, and the planted-churn check fails. The disattenuated pooled NOVCHURN PSP is 0.178 [0.141, 0.214] (approximate, CI not independently re-derived).\n\nBecause the temporal-excess measure is unreliable, the confound analysis cannot adjudicate temporal churn at typical sample sizes (${\\sim}$10 home papers/year). The association that survives behaves like a static dispersion property. Temporal turnover is untested rather than refuted.\n\n\\textbf{Partner decomposition.} The home-only signal is carried by partners from new Leiden communities arriving through mixed-field papers: contrast $C_2$ = +0.102 [+0.069, +0.133] (Holm $p$ = 0.0025), domain Shapley $\\phi$ = +0.132 on the cohort (method = +0.012). Controlling for the share of early bridging papers halves NOVCHURN from 0.118 to 0.056.\n\n\n\\subsection{Exploratory AI-domain stage}\n\nAn exploratory retrospective atlas of 37 AI and computer science concepts was constructed from the large panel, examining how concepts such as deep learning, reinforcement learning and generative adversarial networks evolved through the co-occurrence network before their cross-field diffusion. This atlas is outcome-selected and retrospective; it provides qualitative context but no hypothesis-testing power.\n\n\n\\subsection{Representative case studies}\n\nSeven matched case-study pairs were drawn from the breadth decomposition analysis (Table~\\ref{tab:cases}). These pairs are illustration only; all are descriptive with no $p$-value.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Representative matched case-study pairs contrasting high-breadth and low-breadth concepts matched on early volume. All pairs are illustration; no inferential claim is made.}\n\\label{tab:cases}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{lll}\n\\toprule\nHigh-breadth concept & Low-breadth concept & Group \\\\\n\\midrule\nGraphics processing unit & Vertical-axis wind turbine & Eng \\\\\nShotgun proteomics & Image-guided radiation therapy & BGM \\\\\nNanocarriers & Nanosheet & CS \\\\\nSoft power & Autonomous learning & SOC \\\\\nScopus & Oxygen reduction reaction & CS \\\\\nSclerostin & IgG4-related disease & BGM \\\\\nUser-generated content & Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy & SOC \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_case_study_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Illustrative matched case-study pair from Experiment~12 (case pair 1 of 7): graphics processing unit (GPU; onset $t_0=2008$, high early-neighbourhood openness OPEN) versus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT; $t_0=2009$, low OPEN). Both have an Engineering home field and are matched on early volume and growth. (a)~Number of off-home venue fields each concept has ever entered (solid line, filled markers) and currently retains (dashed line, open markers) in each year from $t_0$ to $t_0+8$; GPU is shown in black and VAWT in grey on a shared axis. By $t_0+2$ GPU had entered 7 off-home fields and VAWT 2; by $t_0+8$ they had entered 11 and 6 and retained 8 and 4. (b,~c)~Topic co-occurrence ego networks over the first three years ($t_0$ to $t_0+2$, all papers). The nodes are the concept's positive-PMI neighbour topics (the concept itself is not drawn), the edges are links between those topics in the 2010--14 topic backbone, node area scales with the number of the concept's papers carrying the topic, and colour gives the topic's Leiden community, named by the plurality OpenAlex field of its topics (plus the runner-up field when it has at least 0.6 times as many). GPU's neighbourhood has 34 topics in 8 communities (density 0.30), led by Engineering \\& Physics, Computer Science and Medicine communities. VAWT's has 12 topics in a single Engineering community (density 0.70). The pair illustrates the openness--breadth association and is not evidence for it (case\\_pairs.json, pair~1).}\n  \\label{fig:case_study}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\n\\subsection{Dead ends and negative results}\n\\label{sec:dead_ends}\n\nTable~\\ref{tab:deadends} lists the principal hypotheses and candidate signals that were tested and did not survive (across five iterations and 21 artifacts).\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Principal dead ends and negative results across five research iterations.}\n\\label{tab:deadends}\n\\small\n\\begin{tabular}{p{4.2cm}p{2.8cm}p{5.2cm}}\n\\toprule\nHypothesis / candidate & Decisive test & Result \\\\\n\\midrule\nNaturalisation gap ($A^*_h$) & Exp.\\ 1 & Fails every clause ($-$0.006) \\\\\n$D_{\\text{ratio}}$, $F_{\\text{res}}$ & Exp.\\ 3 & No candidate survives \\\\\nGateway landing on $O_{2r}$ & Exp.\\ 4, 5 & $\\Delta$AUC $-$0.00001 held-out \\\\\nH3 gateway-weighted landing & Exp.\\ 5 & Pooled CI includes 0 [$-$0.006, 0.065] \\\\\nOrdering (central-first) & Exp.\\ 6, Eval.\\ 2 & MIXED: 32.6\\% of broad concepts; negative lead-lag; pre-trend \\\\\nTwo discrete trajectory classes & Exp.\\ 6, 12 & HMM-vs-DTW ARI 0.094/0.222 \\\\\nAbandonment penalty ($d_{\\text{lost}}$) & Exp.\\ 7 & Specification-dependent: A1 $-$0.007, R4 +0.064, min-cp $-$0.030 \\\\\nVolume-matched retained-frontier contrast & Exp.\\ 7 & Null: $-$0.028 [$-$0.105, +0.046] held-out \\\\\n$O_5$ external recognition & Exp.\\ 8, Eval.\\ 2 & No indicator beats B5 + onset year \\\\\nRescue and relay models & Exp.\\ 6 & Not supported \\\\\nWithin-concept closure & Exp.\\ 11, 15C & Null on DEV; opposite-signed held-out ($-$0.079) \\\\\n$n_{\\text{authors\\_early}}$ for $O_3$ & Exp.\\ 8, 10 & Non-replication on fresh cohort (+0.014) \\\\\nRETENTION\\_RATIO at R2/R3 & Exp.\\ 10 & Null on cohort ($-$0.043 [$-$0.116, 0.031]) \\\\\nTrait prediction (P-B1) & Exp.\\ 15B & Fails: yearly OPEN\\textsubscript{home} ICC 0.34--0.39 \\\\\nFrame~N Cheng reversal & Exp.\\ 13 & Not confirmed ($-$0.064 [$-$0.159, 0.031]) \\\\\nCo-author candidate S & Exp.\\ 8 & Computed; not confirmed for any outcome \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\n\\subsection{What the openness index captures}\n\nThe OPEN index captures the degree to which a concept's early neighbourhood acquires partners from diverse communities rather than reinforcing existing ones. The signal is not demonstrably temporal turnover but a static topical-dispersion property. A within-concept permutation null absorbs the year-to-year component, yet the association persists: concepts whose home-field co-occurrence partners span many communities tend to reach more fields later. This is consistent with \\citeauthor{March1991}'s (\\citeyear{March1991}) exploration--exploitation distinction at the concept level. However, the within-concept closure test is null on DEV and opposite-signed on held-out fields, indicating that openness operates as a between-concept trait rather than as a within-concept causal mechanism.\n\nThe home-only signal (OPEN\\textsubscript{home}) is marginal. The stronger OPEN\\textsubscript{all} signal is partly mechanically coupled: early off-home papers that enter the ego network are a subset of the papers that determine the outcome. OPEN\\textsubscript{sizematch} controls for this coupling and remains significant.\n\n\\subsection{Reconciling consistency and breadth}\n\n\\citet{Cheng2023} found that ideational consistency predicts a concept becoming ``core.'' We replicate their result for volume (+53\\%/SD) but show that, net of volume, the same property predicts \\emph{narrower} cross-field reach. The reversal holds in all five field groups ($I^2 = 0$) and replicates on a fresh cohort. The features predictive of local consolidation and growth are distinct from, and partly opposed to, the features predictive of broad disciplinary spread.\n\n\\subsection{The retained-frontier claim}\n\nThe confirmed field-entry result ($d_0 = 0.322$ on the independent frame) extends the principle of relatedness from economic geography \\citep{Hidalgo2007,Neffke2011} to concept adoption. The result is PARTIAL: the volume-matched contrast is null, and the effect is backbone-specific (it reverses under minimum-conditional-probability proximity). What survives is a PMI-backbone relative-odds effect that cannot be separated from volume. The $I^2$ of 0.92 indicates substantial cross-domain heterogeneity, with Life \\& Environment showing the strongest signal and Mathematics \\& Decision Sciences null.\n\n\\subsection{Limitations}\n\n\\textbf{Effect size.} The OPEN--breadth association is modest. OPEN\\textsubscript{home} adds no forecasting gain over B5 (+0.002 [$-$0.003, +0.008]).\n\n\\textbf{Measurement noise.} Split-half reliability of OPEN\\textsubscript{home} is 0.49. The temporal-excess variants have split-half reliability below 0.05, so temporal versus static dispersion cannot be resolved at available sample sizes.\n\n\\textbf{Vocabulary bias.} The legacy OpenAlex concept vocabulary is survivor-selected. Frame~N is small (636 concepts) with pre-unseal power of 0.47.\n\n\\textbf{Coupling.} About half of the OPEN\\textsubscript{all} signal is mechanical coupling between the ego-network construction (which uses off-home papers) and the breadth outcome. OPEN\\textsubscript{home} is free of this coupling but marginal.\n\n\\textbf{Domain heterogeneity.} Life \\& Environment shows the weakest OPEN signal (PSP +0.042). The retained-field relatedness $I^2$ is 0.92.\n\n\\textbf{Not causal.} Early ego-network openness could reflect a concept's intrinsic generality, the diversity of the research community around it, or the breadth of the problems it addresses.\n\n\\textbf{Prior unsealing.} Held-out outcomes were previously unsealed by two earlier experiments in the same project, so the indicator-screen held-out results are robustness checks.\n\n\n\\section{Conclusions}\n\\label{sec:conclusions}\n\nWe screened 53 early temporal network indicators for predicting the cross-disciplinary breadth of new scientific concepts, using 12{,}499 concepts from the OpenAlex corpus with held-out validation and a fresh cohort confirmation. Seven indicators are confirmed, composing into an openness index that captures topical non-redundancy in a concept's early co-occurrence neighbourhood. The signal is a static between-concept trait; temporal turnover could not be tested at available sample sizes. Early openness predicts breadth; early consolidation predicts volume but not breadth. Concepts spread next to fields related to those currently retaining them, but the pre-registered verdict is PARTIAL: persistence and volume are confounded, and the effect is backbone-specific.\n\n\n\\section*{Declarations}\n\n\\subsection*{Funding}\nNot applicable.\n\n\\subsection*{Conflict of interest}\nThe authors declare no conflict of interest.\n\n\\subsection*{Availability of data and materials}\nThe study uses the publicly available OpenAlex bulk snapshot (2026-09-23). Concept frames, indicator matrices and analysis scripts are available from the corresponding author upon request.\n\n\\subsection*{Code availability}\nAnalysis code is available from the corresponding author upon request.\n\n\\subsection*{Authors' contributions}\nAll authors contributed to the study design, analysis and manuscript preparation.\n\n\\bibliographystyle{plainnat}\n\\bibliography{references}\n\n\\end{document}\n", "numLines": 426, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 426}}

"""Read the run's artifact output files and write the JSON each view of interactive.html embeds."""

from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

ROOT = Path("/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_Id7TLZ6r1C7M/3_invention_loop")

X12 = ROOT / "iter_4/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_12"
X16 = ROOT / "iter_5/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_16"
OUT = Path(__file__).parent / "data"
OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)


def clean(v):
    if isinstance(v, float) and (math.isnan(v) or math.isinf(v)):
        return None
    if hasattr(v, "item"):
        return clean(v.item())
    return v


def dump(name, obj):
    s = json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), allow_nan=False)
    (OUT / f"{name}.json").write_text(s)
    print(f"{name}: {len(s)/1024:.1f} KB")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- evidence synthesis (headline forest)
ev = json.load(open(E4 / "results/evidence_synthesis.json"))
rows = []
for r in ev["rows"]:
    if r["body"] == "B2_HELDOUT_pooled":
        continue  # pooled held-out row is not a body of the six-body synthesis
    row = {"body": r["body"], "feature": r["feature"], "status": r["status"], "onsets": r["onsets"],
           "n_body_rows": r["n_body_rows"], "placebo_p95": r["placebo"]["p95_abs_psp"]}
    for k in ("R0", "R2", "R3"):
        row[k] = {"psp": r[k]["psp"], "ci": r[k]["ci"], "n": r[k]["n"]}
    rows.append(row)
pools = {}
for key, p in ev["pools"].items():
    ns = p["nonselection"]
    pools[key] = {"est": ns["est"], "ci": ns["dl_ci"], "I2": ns["I2"], "k": ns["k"],
                  "bodies": p["nonselection_bodies"], "sign": p["sign_agreement_nonselection"],
                  "selection_est": p["selection_body_estimate"],
                  "shrinkage": p["shrinkage_ratio_selection_over_nonselection"]}
dump("evidence", {"rows": rows, "pools": pools})
pr = pools["OPEN_home|R2"]
print("CHECK pool OPEN_home R2", f"{pr['est']:+.3f} [{pr['ci'][0]:+.3f}, {pr['ci'][1]:+.3f}] I2={pr['I2']} {pr['sign']} shrink={pr['shrinkage']:.2f}",
      "paper: +0.069 [+0.038, +0.100] I2=0 6/6 1.58")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 2015-17 cohort per-concept records
ac = pd.read_parquet(X10 / "data/analysis_cohort.parquet")
pred = pd.read_parquet(X10 / "data/cohort_predictions.parquet")

<body>
<a class="skip" href="#main">Skip to main content</a>
<header class="top">
  <div class="wrap">
    <p class="kicker">Interactive companion to the paper</p>
    <h1>Early co-occurrence network openness predicts cross-disciplinary concept breadth: evidence from 12,499 scientific concepts</h1>
    <p class="byline">AI Inventor</p>
    <div class="links">
      <a class="btn primary" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@fork/run_DVtwwCx0JbFq/paper.pdf">Read the paper (PDF)</a>
      <a class="btn" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them@fork/run_DVtwwCx0JbFq/report.pdf">Read the full research report</a>
      <a class="btn" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8795ea-concepts-spread-once-adopters-make-them/tree/fork/run_DVtwwCx0JbFq">Code repository</a>
    </div>
  </div>
</header>
<nav class="sec" aria-label="Sections">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="#finding">The finding</a></li>
    <li><a href="#method">How it works</a></li>
    <li><a href="#explore">Explore the evidence</a></li>
    <li><a href="#try">Try it</a></li>
    <li><a href="#fails">Where it fails</a></li>
    <li><a href="#about">Links and glossary</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>
<main id="main">
<div class="wrap">

<section class="block" id="finding" aria-labelledby="h-finding">
  <h2 id="h-finding">The finding</h2>
  <div class="grid2">
    <div class="measure">
      <p class="lede">Some new scientific concepts stay inside the field that coined them; others turn up in a dozen fields within a decade. Popularity already predicts much of that difference. The question here is narrower: once early volume, growth and spread are held fixed, does the <em>shape</em> of a concept's early topic neighbourhood say anything more about how broadly it will travel?</p>
      <p>The answer is a small yes. Concepts whose early <button class="term" data-term="home">home-field</button> <button class="term" data-term="cooc">co-occurrence</button> partners are new and span many topic communities, measured by the <button class="term" data-term="OPEN">OPEN index</button>, later reach more fields per paper (<button class="term" data-term="O2r">rarefied breadth</button>) than the <button class="term" data-term="B5">popularity baseline</button> expects.</p>
      <div class="bignum" id="big-num"></div>
      <p class="small" id="big-cap"></p>
      <p>The association has the same sign in every body of concepts not used to choose the index, but it is weak, it adds almost nothing to forecasting accuracy, and it behaves like a fixed property of a concept's topic mix, not like turnover that happens year by year. The paper calls the evidence state a <em>lead</em>.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="view" id="v-headline" aria-labelledby="q-headline">
      <p class="q" id="q-headline">Does the association hold in every body of concepts?</p>
      <p class="qsub">Each row is one body of concepts. The measure is the <button class="term" data-term="PSP">partial Spearman</button> correlation between the index and later breadth after the <button class="term" data-term="rung">control rung</button>. Zero means no information beyond the controls.</p>
      <div class="controls">
        <div><span class="ctl-label" id="lab-feat">Index</span>
          <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-feat" id="ctl-feat"></div></div>
        <div><span class="ctl-label" id="lab-rung">Controls</span>
          <div class="seg" role="radiogroup" aria-labelledby="lab-rung" id="ctl-rung"></div></div>
      </div>
      <div class="controls">
        <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="ctl-dev"> Show the DEV selection body</label>
        <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="ctl-band" checked> Show the placebo null band</label>
      </div>
      <div class="chart" id="chart-headline"></div>
      <div class="legend" id="legend-headline"></div>
      <p class="takeaway" id="tk-headline" aria-live="polite"></p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="block" id="method" aria-labelledby="h-method">
  <h2 id="h-method">How it works: one concept, start to finish</h2>
  <p class="measure">The stepper follows one real record from the fresh 2015&ndash;2017 onset cohort, the only body never used in any earlier step. Every value shown is the value the run stored for this concept, or is computed from those values with the frozen constants the run sealed before looking at outcomes.</p>
  <div class="view" id="v-stepper" aria-labelledby="q-stepper">
    <p class="q" id="q-stepper">What happens to a concept between its first papers and its breadth score?</p>
    <p class="qsub" id="stepper-concept"></p>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-pipeline"></div>
    <ol class="stepper-markers" id="step-markers" aria-label="Stages"></ol>
    <div id="step-live" class="sr" aria-live="polite"></div>
    <h3 id="step-title" tabindex="-1"></h3>
    <div class="stage" id="step-body"></div>
    <div class="navbtns">
      <button type="button" id="step-prev">Previous stage</button>
      <button type="button" id="step-next">Next stage</button>
    </div>
    <p class="small">Left and right arrow keys also move between stages while the stepper has focus.</p>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-stepper"></p>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="block" id="explore" aria-labelledby="h-explore">
  <h2 id="h-explore">Explore the evidence</h2>
  <p class="measure">Four views over the stored records. The first two use the 1,443 concepts of the 2015&ndash;2017 cohort one by one; the third shows how the estimate moves as controls are added; the fourth covers the second research question, how concepts pick the next field they enter.</p>

  <div class="view" id="v-browser" aria-labelledby="q-browser">
    <p class="q" id="q-browser">What does the index do for one concept?</p>
    <p class="qsub">Pick a concept to set its early-window inputs beside two frozen predictions of its later breadth: the <button class="term" data-term="B5">B5</button> baseline alone, and B5 plus OPEN<sub>home</sub>. Both models were fitted on the earlier 12,499-concept frame and never refitted on this cohort.</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <input type="search" id="br-search" placeholder="Search concept name" aria-label="Search concept name">
      <select id="br-group" aria-label="Home group"></select>
      <select id="br-sort" aria-label="Sort order">
        <option value="open_desc">OPEN<sub>home</sub> high to low</option>
        <option value="open_asc">OPEN home low to high</option>
        <option value="y_desc">Breadth high to low</option>
        <option value="gain_desc">OPEN helped most</option>
        <option value="gain_asc">OPEN hurt most</option>
        <option value="name">Name A to Z</option>
      </select>
    </div>
    <div class="controls">
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="br-scored" checked> Only concepts with a breadth outcome and an OPEN<sub>home</sub> score</label>
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="br-hurt"> Only cases where adding OPEN moved the prediction away from the outcome</label>
    </div>
    <div class="browser">
      <div>
        <p class="count" id="br-count" aria-live="polite"></p>
        <div class="list" id="br-list" role="listbox" aria-label="Concepts" tabindex="0"></div>
        <button type="button" class="plain-btn" id="br-more" style="margin-top:8px">Show more</button>
      </div>
      <div id="br-detail" aria-live="polite"></div>
    </div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-browser"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="view" id="v-scatter" aria-labelledby="q-scatter">
    <p class="q" id="q-scatter">Do high-OPEN concepts beat their popularity forecast?</p>
    <p class="qsub">Each point is one cohort concept. Up means the concept reached more fields than the B5 baseline predicted. Drag the cut to split concepts into high and low OPEN<sub>home</sub> and compare how far each group lands above the baseline. Click a point to open it in the browser above.</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <select id="sc-group" aria-label="Home group for scatter"></select>
      <div><label for="sc-cut" class="ctl-label">OPEN<sub>home</sub> cut</label>
        <input type="range" id="sc-cut" min="5" max="95" step="5" value="50" aria-describedby="sc-cut-val">
        <span class="rangeval" id="sc-cut-val"></span></div>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-scatter" ></div>
    <div class="legend">
      <span><i class="sw dot" style="background:var(--accent);opacity:.6"></i>concept</span>
      <span><i class="sw line"></i>B5 prediction (residual 0)</span>
      <span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--warn);height:4px"></i>mean residual within each fifth of OPEN<sub>home</sub></span>
      <span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--ink);width:3px"></i>cut</span>
    </div>
    <div class="stat" id="sc-stats"></div>
    <p class="small">Everything in this view is computed in the page from the stored outcome and the stored B5 prediction. The rank correlation printed here is a plain Spearman correlation with the B5 residual, not the paper's partial Spearman, which residualises on the full control rung.</p>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-scatter"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="view" id="v-ladder" aria-labelledby="q-ladder">
    <p class="q" id="q-ladder">How much of the signal survives stricter controls, and how much is coupling?</p>
    <p class="qsub">On the 2015&ndash;2017 cohort the paper runs a six-rung ladder, R0 to R5, each rung adding controls. Three builds of the index are compared: <button class="term" data-term="OPENhome">home only</button>, <button class="term" data-term="OPENall">all papers</button> and <button class="term" data-term="OPENsize">size-matched</button>.</p>
    <div class="controls" role="group" aria-label="Builds shown">
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" class="ld-b" value="OPEN_home" checked> OPEN<sub>home</sub></label>
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" class="ld-b" value="OPEN_sizematch" checked> OPEN<sub>sizematch</sub></label>
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" class="ld-b" value="OPEN_all" checked> OPEN<sub>all</sub></label>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-ladder"></div>
    <div class="legend" id="legend-ladder"></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-ladder"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="view" id="v-frontier" aria-labelledby="q-frontier">
    <p class="q" id="q-frontier">Do concepts enter fields related to the fields that currently keep them?</p>
    <p class="qsub">A <button class="term" data-term="clogit">conditional logit</button> on field-entry events, fitted on an independent frame of 11,841 concepts. The coefficient <button class="term" data-term="d0">d<sub>0</sub></button> is the change in log-odds of entering a field per SD of relatedness to the <button class="term" data-term="retained">retaining fields</button>, after home relatedness, field size, entered density, gateway centrality, RCA density and volume density.</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="fr-dev"> Show the DEV selection set</label>
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="fr-fail"> Only the pre-registered criteria that failed</label>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-frontier"></div>
    <div class="legend">
      <span><i class="sw dot" style="background:var(--accent)"></i>unit estimate, 95% concept-bootstrap CI</span>
      <span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--ink);transform:rotate(45deg);width:11px;height:11px"></i>DerSimonian&ndash;Laird pool of the four held-out groups</span>
      <span><i class="sw line"></i>d<sub>0</sub> = 0</span>
    </div>
    <h4 style="margin-top:16px">Pre-registered criteria for the frozen verdict</h4>
    <ul class="crit" id="fr-crit"></ul>
    <p class="takeaway warn" id="tk-frontier"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="view" id="v-cases" aria-labelledby="q-cases">
    <p class="q" id="q-cases">What does an open neighbourhood look like next to a closed one?</p>
    <p class="qsub">Seven matched pairs from the breadth-decomposition analysis: in each, two concepts with nearly the same early volume, one high and one low on OPEN<sub>all</sub>. These are illustrations, not evidence.</p>
    <div class="controls"><select id="cs-pair" aria-label="Case pair"></select></div>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-cases"></div>
    <div class="legend">
      <span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></i>high-OPEN concept</span>
      <span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--base)"></i>low-OPEN concept</span>
    </div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-cases"></p>
    <figure>
      <img src="figures/fig_case_study_v0.png" alt="Three panels. Left: step lines of off-home fields ever entered and currently retained from onset to eight years later; graphics processing unit rises to 11 entered and 8 retained, vertical-axis wind turbine to 6 entered and 4 retained. Middle: GPU's early topic neighbourhood, 34 topics in 8 colour-coded communities, density 0.30. Right: VAWT's neighbourhood, 12 topics in a single Engineering community, density 0.70." width="1300" height="558" loading="lazy">
      <figcaption>Illustrative matched case-study pair from Experiment 12 (case pair 1 of 7): graphics processing unit (GPU; onset t<sub>0</sub>=2008, high early-neighbourhood openness OPEN) versus vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT; t<sub>0</sub>=2009, low OPEN). Both have an Engineering home field and are matched on early volume and growth. (a) Number of off-home venue fields each concept has ever entered (solid line, filled markers) and currently retains (dashed line, open markers) in each year from t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+8; GPU is shown in black and VAWT in grey on a shared axis. By t<sub>0</sub>+2 GPU had entered 7 off-home fields and VAWT 2; by t<sub>0</sub>+8 they had entered 11 and 6 and retained 8 and 4. (b, c) Topic co-occurrence ego networks over the first three years (t<sub>0</sub> to t<sub>0</sub>+2, all papers). The nodes are the concept's positive-PMI neighbour topics (the concept itself is not drawn), the edges are links between those topics in the 2010&ndash;14 topic backbone, node area scales with the number of the concept's papers carrying the topic, and colour gives the topic's Leiden community, named by the plurality OpenAlex field of its topics (plus the runner-up field when it has at least 0.6 times as many). GPU's neighbourhood has 34 topics in 8 communities (density 0.30), led by Engineering &amp; Physics, Computer Science and Medicine communities. VAWT's has 12 topics in a single Engineering community (density 0.70). The pair illustrates the openness&ndash;breadth association and is not evidence for it (case_pairs.json, pair 1).</figcaption>
    </figure>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="block" id="try" aria-labelledby="h-try">
  <h2 id="h-try">Try it: compute OPEN<sub>home</sub> yourself</h2>
  <p class="measure">The index is simple enough to run exactly in the page. Each of the six components is clipped to the bounds frozen on the development frame, standardised with the frozen mean and SD, given its sign, and averaged. The two frozen prediction models are linear, so the page reproduces them too. Start from any concept's recorded inputs, then move a component and watch the index and the second prediction respond.</p>
  <div class="view" id="v-try" aria-labelledby="q-try">
    <p class="q" id="q-try">Which components drive a concept's OPEN score, and how far does the score move its forecast?</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <select id="try-pick" aria-label="Concept to load"></select>
      <button type="button" class="plain-btn" id="try-load">Load the concept selected in the browser</button>
      <button type="button" class="plain-btn" id="try-reset">Reset to recorded values</button>
    </div>
    <div class="grid2">
      <div class="sliders" id="try-sliders"></div>
      <div>
        <div class="chart" id="chart-try"></div>
        <div class="legend">
          <span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></i>signed z raises OPEN</span>
          <span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--warn)"></i>signed z lowers OPEN</span>
          <span><i class="sw line"></i>OPEN<sub>home</sub> (mean)</span>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="stat" id="try-stats"></div>
    <p class="small" id="try-check" aria-live="polite"></p>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-try"></p>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="block" id="fails" aria-labelledby="h-fails">
  <h2 id="h-fails">Where it fails</h2>
  <p class="measure">Three failures carry the most weight. The forecasting gain is close to zero. The temporal reading of the index, that concepts spread because their partners <em>keep changing</em>, could not be tested. And the field-entry result misses one of its own pre-registered criteria.</p>
  <div class="controls">
    <button type="button" class="plain-btn" id="goto-hurt">Show the cohort concepts where OPEN hurt the forecast</button>
  </div>

  <div class="view" id="v-noise" aria-labelledby="q-noise">
    <p class="q" id="q-noise">Is the churn signal real turnover, or a property of small yearly samples?</p>
    <p class="qsub"><button class="term" data-term="NOVCHURN">NOVCHURN</button> combines neighbourhood novelty and low <button class="term" data-term="persist">edge persistence</button>. Each row rebuilds it under a different noise control, pooled over four bodies at rung R2. Tick a control to add its row.</p>
    <div class="controls" role="group" aria-label="Noise controls shown" id="nz-ctl"></div>
    <div class="chart" id="chart-noise"></div>
    <div class="legend">
      <span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--base)"></i>raw NOVCHURN (reference)</span>
      <span><i class="sw dot" style="background:var(--accent)"></i>noise-controlled variant, 95% CI</span>
      <span><i class="sw line"></i>zero</span>
    </div>
    <p class="takeaway warn" id="tk-noise"></p>
  </div>

  <div class="view">
    <h3>What the paper says it does not show</h3>
    <ul class="measure">
      <li><strong>Effect size.</strong> OPEN<sub>home</sub> adds no forecasting gain over B5: <span id="lim-gain"></span> in Spearman on the fresh cohort.</li>
      <li><strong>Measurement noise.</strong> Split-half reliability of OPEN<sub>home</sub> is 0.49. The temporal-excess variants have split-half reliability below 0.05, so temporal versus static dispersion cannot be resolved at available sample sizes.</li>
      <li><strong>Vocabulary bias.</strong> The legacy OpenAlex concept vocabulary is survivor-selected. The vocabulary-free Frame N is small (636 concepts), with pre-unseal power of 0.47; its frozen verdict is PARTIAL.</li>
      <li><strong>Coupling.</strong> About half of the OPEN<sub>all</sub> signal is mechanical coupling between the ego-network construction, which uses off-home papers, and the breadth outcome. OPEN<sub>home</sub> is free of this coupling but marginal.</li>
      <li><strong>Domain heterogeneity.</strong> Life &amp; Environment shows the weakest OPEN signal in the paper's indicator screen; the retained-frontier coefficient has I<sup>2</sup> = 0.92 across held-out groups.</li>
      <li><strong>Not causal.</strong> Early openness could reflect a concept's intrinsic generality, the diversity of the research community around it, or the breadth of the problems it addresses. A within-concept closure test is null on DEV and opposite-signed on held-out fields, so openness is a between-concept trait, not a within-concept mechanism.</li>
      <li><strong>Prior unsealing.</strong> Held-out outcomes were read by two earlier experiments, so all non-selection bodies except the 2015&ndash;2017 cohort are robustness checks, and the six-body pool is descriptive.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</section>
</div>
</main>
